results.query: We charter about 220 hours annually today, mostly between Dallas, Chicago, New York, and Europe. Some trips are just 3 executives, others are 12-person deal teams. At what point does fractional stop making sense?
results.answer_preview:
Ownership Economics (simulated):

- Utilization: fractional/charter-adjacent (150–250 hr/year)
- Structure: fractional program
- Planning economics @ 220 hr/year: ~$4,200/hr variable + ~$850,000/yr fixed → ~$8,063/hr all-in (directional, not a quote).

Analysis: Dispatch tradeoff: charter/card preserves peak-day flexibility without fixed crew idle; ownership or higher fractional share buys schedule control when ad-hoc lift fails . Capital efficiency: compare burdened all-in hourly (fixed + variable amortized) to fractional card pricing at your peak month — crossover is often utilization-driven
